Computing & programming

project noun

also undertaking

classical

opus, operis n.

noun, third declension

work or undertaking

Our everyday choice for a project being carried out. Plural opera, operum n. pl. Recovered from our 24 September 2026 discussion: both words were proposed, and Jack used Opus incipiāmus. These are contextual choices, not a claim that either word always corresponds to every English use of “project.”

Examples

  • Opus incipiāmus.

    Let’s begin the project.composed

  • Hoc opus suscipiāmus.

    Let’s undertake this project.composed

  • In hōc opere labōrō.

    I’m working on this project.composed

Other words

  • cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n. — plan, intention or design

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    Useful when the planned undertaking is the focus.

See also plan.

SourcesLewis & Short: opus · Lewis & Short: consilium. Dictionary links support the component words; the modern technical expressions are labelled separately.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
